title: Fracture / Splinting Guide

changelog.change: Initial entry — region → splint type / position / neurovascular check / red flags.

purpose: Bone/region selector → splint type, position, the neurovascular check that matters for that region, and the red flags that mean emergent ortho.

nodes.body: Buddy tape or aluminium splint, position of function. Check: digital capillary refill, 2-point discrimination. Red flags → ortho: rotational deformity, open fracture.
Sugar-tong or volar/dorsal splint. Wrist 20-30° extension, MCP 70-90° flexion, IP extension. Check: median / ulnar / radial nerve function. Red flag: compartment syndrome signs.
Sugar-tong splint. Elbow 90°, forearm neutral. Check: radial pulse, median / ulnar / radial nerve. Red flags: open fracture, neurovascular compromise.
Posterior long-arm splint at 90° flexion. Check: radial pulse, median / ulnar / radial nerve. Red flag: brachial artery injury — high suspicion in supracondylar fractures.
Coaptation splint or sugar-tong, arm adducted, elbow 90°. Check: radial nerve (wrist drop). Red flag: radial nerve palsy — common with midshaft fractures.
Buddy tape, neutral. Check: capillary refill. Red flag: open fracture.
Posterior splint ± stirrup, neutral / 90°. Check: dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses. Red flags: compartment syndrome, dislocation.
Long-leg posterior splint, knee slight flexion, ankle neutral. Check: distal pulses, compartment exam. Red flag: compartment syndrome — high index of suspicion.
Knee immobiliser, full extension or slight flexion. Check: popliteal pulse, peroneal nerve (foot drop). Red flag: vascular injury with knee dislocation — needs a vascular workup even if reduced.
Traction splint as a prehospital / ED bridge, traction applied. Check: femoral and distal pulses. Red flag: high-energy mechanism — assess for associated injuries.

checklist: Neurovascular status assessed and DOCUMENTED before any manipulation
Adequate analgesia / procedural sedation before reduction attempts
Splint applied with adequate padding — avoid acute circumferential casting (swelling risk)
Neurovascular status re-checked and re-DOCUMENTED after splinting
Discharge: RICE, elevation above heart level, return precautions (numbness, worsening pain, colour change, fever)
Ortho follow-up ~ 5-7 days for most closed fractures; sooner for intra-articular or displaced
